newsitem.title: HONG KONG: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - APP out, others on outlook.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - APP out, others on outlook.

text.p: APP Global Finance (III) brought its US$400 million floating rate note issue to the Asian debt markets on Tuesday and bankers said that other big-ticket deals are on the outlook.
Meanwhile, Thai credits traded in the secondary markets were little moved by news Standard and Poor's Corp had affirmed the sovereign's ratings while cutting a few of the banks.
S&P has long made it clear that it disagrees with Moody's Investors Service on the creditworthiness of the sovereign. Moody's downgraded Thailand on February 14.
And most rating agencies, including Thailand's TRIS, have been negative on the banks.
"There wasn't any physical selling of the bank issues, but people have long been cautious on Thailand," said a trader at a U.S. bank.
"But we keep hearing that some credit departments are saying that they are not going to approve any more credit lines to Thai markets," she said.
In the primary markets, the APP notes, which are due April 2002, were launched at par and have an indicated coupon range of 400-425 basis points over six-month LIBOR.
Fees are 200 basis points for lead managers committing US$20 million or more for an all-in yield of 440 to 460 basis points.
Security is provided by pledge of shares in APP Finance (III) Mauritius Ltd that can be exchanged into preferred shares of Asia Pulp and Paper.

The syndication style, where a loan-style issue is launched with an indicated range and is priced weeks later based on demand, is unusual in Asia but typical of Peregrine Fixed Income, which is the arranger of this deal.

Bankers said that APP is a respectable credit and the issue's high yield makes it attractive. A similar deal launched by UBS last year was heavily oversubscribed and increased to US$600 million from US$500 million.
Bankers said one of the downsides of the issue is its lack of rarity value, as APP units are regular borrowers.
Sino Commercial Properties Funding's US$300 million mortgage backed FRN was priced during London hours.

The deal, which has an expected final of five years, pays a coupon of 85 basis points over LIBOR and was priced and re-offered at 99.70 to give a discount margin of 90 basis points. Morgan Stanley International was lead manager.
Looking ahead, a US$500 million global bond for Export-Import Bank of Korea will be launched via Lehman Brothers after this week's roadshows.
Korea Telecom is forecast to follow Kexim with a bond issue to be lead by Salomon Brothers. Bankers also are awaiting a mandate from Korea Mobile Telecom.
Morgan Stanley is tipped to be the winner of a bond mandate from Bank of China, but the investment bank declined comment.

Tenaga may also have bestowed the mandate for its expected US$400-500 million Yankee bond. A European bank with a presence in Labuan, Malaysia's offshore banking center, may have taken the prize, bankers said.
There is also talk that another Malaysian borrower is peeking at the market for a debut issue.
